watch_outs.text: Women in regular employment with Central Government, State Government, PSU, or receiving similar benefits under any law are not entitled to PMMVY benefits.
watch_outs.quote: All pregnant women and lactating mothers in regular employment with the Central Government or State Government or Public Sector Undertaking or those who are in receipt of similar benefits under any law for the time being in force shall not be entitled to benefits under PMMVY.

watch_outs.text: Apply within 2 years from the date of Last Menstrual Period.
watch_outs.quote: Yes, the beneficiary can only apply for the scheme within 2 years from the date of beneficiary’s Last Menstrual Period subject to the eligibility conditions of the scheme.

watch_outs.text: If the child does not survive, the beneficiary is not eligible for benefits under PMMVY for further pregnancies as she has already claimed the installments.
watch_outs.quote: No, in an unfortunate event that the child does not survive, the beneficiary is not eligible for benefits under PMMVY for further pregnancies as she has already claimed the installments.

watch_outs.text: If already availing paid maternity leave from employer, you are not eligible for this scheme.
watch_outs.quote: No, if you are already availing any paid maternity scheme or a paid maternity leave from your employer, then in that case you won’t be eligible for this scheme.

watch_outs.text: LMP date from MCP Card is mandatory to claim the 1st and 2nd installment; without it only the 3rd installment can be claimed if conditions are met.
watch_outs.quote: Yes. The LMP Date, as found in the Mother Child Protection (MCP) Card is mandatory to claim the 1st and 2nd installment. If LMP Date is not provided, the beneficiary is not eligible to claim the 1st and 2nd installment and can claim only the 3rd installment provided she fulfils the conditionality for availing third installment of the Scheme.

faq.q: By when can I claim the second installment of the cash incentive?
faq.a: The 2nd installment can be claimed 180 days after the Last Menstrual Period (LMP) of the applicant.
faq.quote: The 2nd installment can be claimed 180 days after the Last Menstrual Period (LMP) of the applicant.

faq.q: Does this scheme provide any additional coverages?
faq.a: Apart from the three installments to be claimed within 150 days, 180 days, and at childbirth, the scheme does not offer additional coverages.
faq.quote: Apart from the three installments to be claimed within 150 days, 180 days, and at childbirth, the scheme does not offer additional coverages.

faq.q: Does the benefit under PMMVY continue in case of death?
faq.a: No, in an unfortunate event that the child does not survive, the beneficiary is not eligible for benefits under PMMVY for further pregnancies as she has already claimed the installments.
faq.quote: No, in an unfortunate event that the child does not survive, the beneficiary is not eligible for benefits under PMMVY for further pregnancies as she has already claimed the installments.

faq.q: Will the beneficiary get the benefit in case of miscarriage or stillbirth?
faq.a: The beneficiary will receive the installments until the pregnancy is active; the date of miscarriage will be a factor in deciding whether the benefit will continue or not.
faq.quote: The beneficiary will receive the installments until the pregnancy is active. Since the benefit is paid out in three installments depending upon the pregnancy milestones, the beneficiary will receive at least two installments in case of stillbirth. The date of miscarriage will be a factor in deciding whether the benefit will continue or not.

faq.q: I have received only the first installment under IGMSY. Can I claim the remaining installments under PMMVY?
faq.a: Beneficiaries who have received only the first installment under the old MBP (IGMSY) scheme can claim only third installment under the PMMVY scheme, subject to meeting the criteria of PMMVY.
faq.quote: Beneficiaries who have received only the first installment under the old MBP (IGMSY) scheme can claim only third installment under the PMMVY scheme, subject to meeting the criteria of PMMVY.

faq.q: I am expecting twins, am I also eligible for this scheme?
faq.a: Yes, you are eligible to avail the benefits under this scheme.
faq.quote: Yes, you are eligible to avail the benefits under this scheme.

faq.q: What does NSAP stand for and when was it launched?
faq.a: NSAP stands for National Social Assistance Programme and was launched on 15th August 1995.
faq.quote: NSAP stands for National Social Assistance Programme. NSAP was launched on 15th August 1995.

faq.q: What is the pension amount under IGNOAPS and is it restricted to one person in a family?
faq.a: The central contribution is Rs. 200 per month per beneficiary up to 79 years and Rs.500 per month per beneficiary from 80 years onwards; all persons aged 60 years in a BPL family are eligible.
faq.quote: The central contribution of pension under the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) is Rs. 200/- per month per beneficiary up to 79 years and Rs.500/- per month per beneficiary from 80 year onwards and the State Governments may contribute over and above to this amount. At present old age beneficiaries are getting anywhere between Rs. 200/- to Rs. 1000/- depending on the State Contribution. All the persons who are 60 years of age in a BPL family are eligible to get an old age pension.

faq.q: Who implements NSAP?
faq.a: NSAP schemes are mainly implemented by Social Welfare Departments in the States, with specific departments in some states, and extends to both rural and urban areas.
faq.quote: The NSAP Schemes are mainly implemented by the Social Welfare Departments in the States. But NSAP is implemented by Rural Development Department in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Meghalaya and West Bengal; by the Department of Women & Child Development in Orissa and Puducherry; by the Revenue Department in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and by the Department of Labour Employment & Training in Jharkhand. The NSAP extends to both the rural as well as urban areas

faq.q: What is the basic eligibility criterion under NSAP?
faq.a: The applicant must belong to a Below Poverty Line family according to Government of India criteria.
faq.quote: For getting benefits under NSAP the applicant must belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family according to the criteria prescribed by the Govt. of India.

faq.q: How are beneficiaries identified in rural areas?
faq.a: New beneficiaries are identified from the BPL list prepared by States/UTs as per Ministry of Rural Development guidelines for the BPL Census 2002.
faq.quote: As per the revised eligibility criteria, new beneficiaries will be identified from the BPL list prepared by the States/UTs as per guidelines issued by the Ministry of Rural Development (MORD) for the BPL Census 2002.

faq.q: What is the funding pattern under NSAP?
faq.a: Under NSAP 100 percent Central Assistance is extended to the States/UTs to provide benefits.
faq.quote: Under NSAP 100 percent Central Assistance is extended to the States/UTs to provide the benefits in accordance with the norms, guidelines, and conditions laid down by the Central Government.

faq.q: Is there any provision of default nominee or blood relation?

Death due to accidental causes will be covered from day one of insurance coverage.

watch_outs.text: An individual with multiple bank accounts in one or different banks is eligible to join through one savings bank account only.
watch_outs.quote: In case of multiple bank accounts held by an individual in one or different banks, the person would be eligible to join the scheme through one saving bank account only.

watch_outs.text: The cover is valid for one year from 1st June to 31st May on payment of annual premium and is renewable from year to year.
watch_outs.quote: Coverage under PMJJBY is valid for one year from 1st June to 31st May on payment of annual premium.

watch_outs.text: Delayed enrolment for prospective cover is possible with reduced premium depending on the month of enrolment: June–August ₹436, September–November ₹342, December–February ₹228, March–May ₹114.
watch_outs.quote: Delayed enrolment for prospective cover is possible on payment of premium as described below – a) For enrolment in June, July and August – Full Annual Premium of Rs.436/- is payable. b) For enrolment in September, October, and November –premium of Rs. 342/- is payable c) For enrolment in December, January and February –premium of Rs. 228/- is payable. d) For enrolment in March, April and May –premium of Rs. 114/- is payable.

watch_outs.text: Applicants must be between 18 and 50 years of age and hold an individual bank or post office account.
watch_outs.quote: The age of the applicant must be between 18 to 50 Years. The applicant must hold an individual bank / post office account.

faq.q: How do I pay the premium for PMJJBY?
faq.a: The premium will be deducted from the account holder’s bank / Post office account through ‘auto debit’ facility.
faq.quote: The premium will be deducted from the account holder’s bank / Post office account through ‘auto debit’ facility.

faq.q: What is the validity of the insurance cover in PMJJBY?
faq.a: Coverage under PMJJBY is valid for one year from 1st June to 31st May on payment of annual premium.
faq.quote: Coverage under PMJJBY is valid for one year from 1st June to 31st May on payment of annual premium.

faq.q: Is delayed enrolment for prospective cover possible under this scheme?
faq.a: Yes. Delayed enrolment for prospective cover is possible on payment of premium: June–August ₹436, September–November ₹342, December–February ₹228, March–May ₹114.
faq.quote: Delayed enrolment for prospective cover is possible on payment of premium as described below – a) For enrolment in June, July and August – Full Annual Premium of Rs.436/- is payable. b) For enrolment in September, October, and November –premium of Rs. 342/- is payable c) For enrolment in December, January and February –premium of Rs. 228/- is payable. d) For enrolment in March, April and May –premium of Rs. 114/- is payable.

faq.q: If I decide to exit the scheme, is there any possibility that I can rejoin at a later point of time?
faq.a: Yes. One can enroll again under the same conditions of eligibility stipulated in the Scheme.
faq.quote: Yes. One can enroll again under the same conditions of eligibility stipulated in the Scheme.

faq.q: Who will offer / administer the scheme?
faq.a: The scheme would be offered / administered through Insurance companies willing to offer the product with necessary approvals on similar terms, in collaboration with participating Banks.
faq.quote: The scheme would be offered / administered through Insurance companies willing to offer the product with necessary approvals on similar terms, in collaboration with participating Banks. Participating banks will be free to engage any such insurance company for implementing the scheme for their subscribers.

faq.q: What is the minimum eligibility to subscribe to PMJJBY?
faq.a: All savings bank account holders in the age 18 to 50 years in participating banks will be entitled to join; an individual with multiple bank accounts is eligible through one savings bank account only.
faq.quote: All savings bank account holders in the age 18 to 50 years in participating banks will be entitled to join. In case of multiple bank accounts held by an individual in one or different banks, the person would be eligible to join the scheme through one saving bank account only.

faq.q: Who can claim insurance benefit in case of death of the bank account holder who gave the enrolment form?
faq.a: Claim can be filed by the nominee/appointee as per the enrolment form or by the legal heir/s if no nomination was made.
faq.quote: In case of death of the Account holder who enrolled in the scheme, claim can be filed by the nominee/appointee as per the enrolment form or by the legal heir/s in case there is no nomination made by the subscriber bank account holder.

faq.q: What is the mode of payment of the claim amount?
faq.a: Disability claim is credited to the insured account holder's bank account; death claims are remitted to the nominee/legal heir(s)' bank account.
faq.quote: Disability Claim will be credited in the bank account of the insured bank account holder. Death claims will be remitted to the bank account of the nominee / legal heir(s).

faq.q: Is it necessary to report accidents to police and obtain FIR for claiming benefits under the policy?
faq.a: Yes for road, rail, vehicular accidents, drowning, death involving crime; for snake bite or fall from tree, cause should be supported by immediate hospital record.
faq.quote: In case of incidents like Road, Rail and similar vehicular accidents, drowning, death involving any crime etc., the accident should be reported to police. In case of incidents like snake bite, fall from tree etc., the cause should be supported by immediate hospital record.

faq.q: Can an account holder get claim from more than one bank where he has enrolled and premium has been debited?
faq.a: No, the insured/nominee shall be eligible for one claim only.
faq.quote: No. The insured/ Nominee shall be eligible for one claim only.

faq.q: Can an individual join PMSBY from multiple bank accounts?
faq.a: No, the person would be eligible to join through one bank/post office account only.
faq.quote: No. In case of multiple bank accounts held by an individual in one or different banks, the person would be eligible to join the scheme through one bank/post office account only.

faq.q: What is the minimum and maximum age limit for entry into this scheme?
faq.a: Individuals aged between 18 years (completed) and 70 years (age nearer birthday) are eligible.
faq.quote: Individuals aged between 18 years (completed) and 70 years (age nearer birthday) are eligible for this scheme.

faq.q: What is the maximum age for opening a Sukanya Samriddhi account?
faq.a: The girl child must not have attained the age of 10 years on the date the account is opened.
faq.quote: The girl child must not have attained the age of 10 years on the date the account is opened.

faq.q: Can a father open a Sukanya Samriddhi account?
faq.a: A father can open the account as a natural guardian, provided the girl child meets the eligibility conditions.
faq.quote: A father can open the account as a natural guardian, provided the girl child meets the eligibility conditions.

faq.q: Can a mother open an SSY account?
faq.a: A mother can also open the account as a natural guardian of an eligible girl child.
faq.quote: A mother can also open the account as a natural guardian of an eligible girl child.

faq.q: Can a legal guardian open the account?
faq.a: The rules allow a natural or legal guardian to open a Sukanya Samriddhi account in the name of an eligible girl child.
faq.quote: The rules allow a natural or legal guardian to open a Sukanya Samriddhi account in the name of an eligible girl child.

faq.q: Can an account be opened for a boy child?
faq.a: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is specifically designed for eligible girl children.
faq.quote: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is specifically designed for eligible girl children.

faq.q: How many Sukanya Samriddhi accounts can one girl have?
faq.a: Only one account can be opened in the name of a girl child under the scheme.
faq.quote: Only one account can be opened in the name of a girl child under the scheme. Opening multiple accounts for the same girl is not permitted.
